say: Research interpretation (unproven): The strongest Riga signal is the municipal notice announcing traffic changes around Jāņa Čakstes gatve and Vienības gatve. It supports relevant briefing material, not recurring courier pain or demand. The first audience hypothesis is couriers whose routes cross that area, segmented by bicycle, scooter or car. Nobody pays in the proposed €0 pilot. Later payer candidates are individual couriers or delivery-fleet operators, but no supplied receipt establishes their willingness to pay. uncertainty: Couriers repeatedly crossing the affected area may value checked Latvian/Russian summaries over their existing information methods; route exposure, language preference and recurrence remain unproven.
Individual couriers might pay if the briefing demonstrably saves effort; fleet operators might pay if it improves dispatch information. Neither payer hypothesis has direct source support.

Proposed test, not yet run: approach ten stationary couriers with explicit opt-in, record vehicle type, affected routes and current information methods, then offer two independently checked briefings compared with the original notice. No interviews, customer contact, repeat-use observations or payment tests have occurred.
Whether the announced restriction remains active, which vehicle types it affects, and whether enough relevant notices exist for a daily service.
dissent: A traffic-change notice establishes an information event, not a recurring customer problem; a daily briefing could add reading rather than save time.
Four free repeat requests would justify further investigation, not a business case. Conversely, a tightly bounded free usefulness test need not wait for a confirmed payer.
